output.executive_summary:
The Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM), a Syrian-led nonprofit consortium registered in Türkiye and operating across Syria, submits this concept note as lead applicant for Lot 3 of EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY — Promotion of and support to media freedom and pluralism in Syria. Since its founding in 2018, CSIM has built a distinctive operational architecture combining an Istanbul headquarters with field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli, enabling sustained engagement with Syrian journalists across multiple governorates. With a network of vetted Syrian journalists, multilingual production capacity in Arabic, Kurdish, English, and Turkish, and a track record of four sub-million-EUR grants delivered on time under SIDA, Free Press Unlimited, and Internews frameworks, CSIM is among the few Syrian-led organizations capable of leading a Lot 3 action at the required scale and quality.

CSIM's proposed action directly addresses all three Lot 3 priorities: strengthening independent media and journalists to exercise fundamental freedoms; providing effective protection and support to journalists, bloggers, and other media workers; and raising public awareness on the centrality of media freedom in Syria's transitional moment. The organization's information-integrity programming, editorial coaching for newsrooms in exile, and multi-platform content production capabilities are precisely calibrated to the post-Assad transitional context, where independent Syrian media must simultaneously rebuild operational capacity, resist disinformation, and serve diverse communities across a fractured information landscape. CSIM's Arabic and Kurdish language capacity ensures genuine reach to both Arab and Kurdish-speaking communities, directly addressing the call's cross-cutting minority rights and inclusion requirements.

The fixed grant amount for Lot 3 is EUR 675,000, with EU co-financing of up to 90 percent of total eligible costs for an applicant established in Türkiye. CSIM's clean KPMG Türkiye audit (2024) and established donor-reporting systems against EU and US humanitarian frameworks provide the financial management assurance the European Commission requires. CSIM intends to identify and contract one EU-eligible co-applicant to strengthen geographic coverage inside Syria and to demonstrate consortium depth, while retaining lead applicant responsibility for financial management, reporting, and strategic direction. Completion of PADOR registration before the 18 May 2026 deadline is the single most urgent administrative action required and is already in progress.
technical_approach: Context analysis and needs assessment. CSIM's proposed action is grounded in a rigorous analysis of Syria's post-December 2024 transitional media environment. The collapse of the Assad regime has created both an unprecedented opening for independent journalism and acute new risks: a fragmented information ecosystem, the proliferation of armed-group-affiliated outlets, residual self-censorship among journalists conditioned by 14 years of repression, and the physical insecurity of reporters operating in areas with contested authority. CSIM's field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli provide real-time situational awareness across Northwest Syria, the Kurdish-administered northeast, and diaspora media hubs. This distributed presence will be used to conduct a structured needs assessment in the first 60 days of the action, mapping active independent media outlets, identifying protection gaps, and profiling the training needs of journalists across target governorates. The assessment will explicitly disaggregate data by gender, ethnicity, and geographic location to ensure the action's design is evidence-based and inclusive.

Intervention logic and results chain. The action's theory of change holds that a free, professional, and protected Syrian media sector is both a prerequisite for and a product of democratic transition. Inputs — financial resources, CSIM's institutional expertise, and the co-applicant's in-country presence — will fund a structured sequence of activities: capacity-building training for journalists and editors; deployment of a journalist protection protocol and rapid-response support mechanism; production and distribution of public-awareness content on media freedom; and institutional strengthening of at least six independent Syrian newsrooms. These activities will generate measurable outputs including the number of journalists trained, protection cases supported, newsrooms receiving editorial coaching, and public-awareness products disseminated. Outputs will accumulate into outcomes — improved journalistic standards, reduced vulnerability of media workers, and increased public understanding of media freedom — contributing to the global objective of sustainable and equitable development and full enjoyment of human rights in Syria.

Workstream 1 — Journalist capacity building and editorial coaching. CSIM will deliver a structured training curriculum for Syrian journalists covering investigative reporting, digital security, verification and fact-checking, trauma-informed reporting, and editorial ethics. Training will be delivered in Arabic and Kurdish through a blended modality combining in-person workshops at CSIM's Gaziantep and Qamishli nodes with remote coaching sessions accessible to journalists inside Syria. CSIM's network of vetted Syrian journalists will serve as both trainees and, where appropriate, peer trainers, building sustainable internal capacity within the Syrian media sector. Editorial coaching will be provided to at least six independent newsrooms, with CSIM's experienced editorial staff embedded as advisers for defined periods. All training materials will be developed with gender-sensitive and minority-inclusive framing, and at least 40 percent of training participants will be women journalists.

Workstream 2 — Journalist protection and rapid-response support. CSIM will operationalize a journalist protection mechanism drawing on its existing relationships with vetted journalists across Syrian governorates. The mechanism will include a secure reporting channel for threats and incidents, a rapid-response protocol linking CSIM's Istanbul coordination hub with field nodes, and a small emergency fund to support journalists facing acute security threats, legal harassment, or forced displacement. CSIM will document all protection cases in a structured database, producing quarterly protection monitoring reports that will contribute to the broader evidence base on media freedom conditions in Syria. The protection mechanism will be designed in consultation with international press freedom organizations and will align with established frameworks such as the UN Plan of Action on the Safety of Journalists. The co-applicant will be selected in part for their capacity to extend this protection reach into governorates where CSIM's direct field presence is limited.

Workstream 3 — Public awareness and media freedom advocacy. CSIM will design and implement a multi-platform public awareness campaign on the centrality of media freedom to Syria's democratic transition. Content will be produced in Arabic and Kurdish and distributed across social media platforms, partner radio stations, and community networks. The campaign will include explainer content on journalists' rights, the role of independent media in accountability, and the risks of disinformation. CSIM's multi-platform content production capability will be deployed to ensure high-quality, contextually appropriate materials that resonate with Syrian audiences inside the country and in the diaspora. At least two public events — one online and one in-person at a field node — will be organized to convene journalists, civil society actors, and community representatives around media freedom themes. Campaign reach and engagement will be tracked through platform analytics and community feedback mechanisms.

Cross-cutting issues integration. Gender equality will be mainstreamed throughout the action: the needs assessment will include a gender analysis of the Syrian media sector; training curricula will address gender-based threats to women journalists; and the editorial coaching programme will support newsrooms in developing gender-sensitive editorial policies. Minority rights will be addressed through the Kurdish-language programming strand and through deliberate outreach to journalists from minority communities including Kurds, Christians, Druze, and other groups. Youth engagement will be built into the training programme through a dedicated strand for emerging journalists under 30. The action will also address the digital dimension of media freedom, including online harassment, surveillance, and platform-based censorship, reflecting the EU's priority of safeguarding fundamental freedoms in the digital environment. Environmental and climate reporting will be included as a thematic module within the training curriculum, given the growing relevance of climate-related displacement and resource conflict in Syria.

Partnership and co-applicant strategy. CSIM intends to identify one EU-eligible co-applicant with demonstrated in-country presence in Syria, complementary sectoral expertise in press freedom or digital rights, and an established relationship with Syrian civil society. The co-applicant will be responsible for extending the action's geographic reach into governorates not directly covered by CSIM's existing field nodes, and for contributing to the journalist protection mechanism. CSIM will retain lead applicant responsibility for financial management, donor reporting, and strategic oversight. The partnership will be governed by a co-applicant agreement specifying roles, responsibilities, financial flows, and reporting obligations. Potential co-applicant profiles include EU-registered press freedom organizations with Syria programming experience; the bid manager should identify and approach at least two candidates before the concept note submission deadline.

Monitoring, evaluation, and quality assurance. CSIM will implement a results-based monitoring framework aligned with the action's intervention logic. Key performance indicators will be defined for each output and outcome, with baseline values established during the initial needs assessment. Data collection will be conducted by CSIM's field staff using standardized tools, with quarterly internal reviews and a mid-term external review at month 12. CSIM's donor-reporting experience against EU and US humanitarian frameworks — including SIDA, Free Press Unlimited, and Internews — provides an established quality assurance infrastructure. Financial management will follow CSIM's KPMG-audited internal control procedures, with segregation of duties between programme and finance staff. All project documentation will be maintained in a secure digital archive accessible to the contracting authority on request. A final external evaluation will be commissioned in the last quarter of the action to assess impact and generate lessons learned for the Syrian media development sector.

output.cover_letter_draft:
[DATE]

To the Evaluation Committee,
European Commission — EU Delegation to Syria
Call for Proposals EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY
Support to Justice, Freedom of Expression and Social Cohesion in Syria — Lot 3

Dear Members of the Evaluation Committee,

The Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM) is pleased to submit this concept note in response to Lot 3 of the Call for Proposals EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY, Promotion of and Support to Media Freedom and Pluralism in Syria. CSIM is a Syrian-led nonprofit consortium founded in 2018, registered in Türkiye with legal personality, and operating across Syrian governorates through field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli. We write with a deep sense of purpose at this historic moment: the fall of the Assad regime on 8 December 2024 has opened a fragile but genuine window for independent Syrian journalism to take root, and CSIM exists precisely to ensure that Syrian journalists and media workers can seize that opportunity safely, professionally, and sustainably. We believe this call represents the most strategically significant EU investment in Syrian media freedom since the beginning of the conflict, and we are committed to delivering results that justify that investment.

CSIM brings to Lot 3 a combination of capabilities that is rare among organizations working on Syrian media development. Our network of vetted Syrian journalists spans multiple governorates and language communities, enabling us to deliver training, protection support, and editorial coaching in Arabic and Kurdish to journalists who are often beyond the reach of internationally headquartered organizations. Since 2018, we have delivered four grants totalling under EUR 4 million on time and without audit qualification, under frameworks established by SIDA, Free Press Unlimited, and Internews. Our 2024 audit by KPMG Türkiye confirmed clean financial management. We have developed information-integrity programming, multi-platform content production, and journalist protection protocols that are directly applicable to the three priorities of Lot 3: strengthening independent media, protecting journalists and media workers, and raising public awareness on media freedom. We intend to submit this application as lead applicant in consortium with one EU-eligible co-applicant with complementary in-country presence, ensuring that the action achieves genuine geographic reach across Syria's diverse and complex media landscape.

We respectfully request that the Evaluation Committee give full consideration to this concept note. CSIM is prepared to provide any additional documentation, clarification, or supporting evidence that the contracting authority may require during the evaluation process. We are committed to full compliance with all administrative, eligibility, and ethical requirements of this call, and we look forward to the opportunity to contribute to Syria's media freedom and democratic transition under EU partnership. We are available to attend the information sessions on 21 and 22 April 2026 and will register by the 15 April deadline.

Yours sincerely,

[Name of Executive Director / Authorized Representative]
Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM)
[Address: Istanbul headquarters]
[Email]
[Telephone]
PADOR Registration Number: [to be inserted upon completion]
financial_template_notes: Fixed grant amount for Lot 3 is EUR 675,000 — this is both the minimum and maximum EU contribution. The total eligible cost of the action must therefore be sized so that EUR 675,000 represents between 70% and 90% of total eligible costs. At 90% co-financing (applicable to CSIM as a Türkiye-registered entity), total eligible costs = EUR 750,000, with CSIM contributing EUR 75,000 (10%). At 70% co-fi

Co-financing sources must not come from the EU general budget or the European Development Fund. Eligible co-financing sources include CSIM's own reserves, contributions from non-EU donors, or in-kind contributions valued at market rates. Document the source and availability of co-financing in the budget narrative.

Key cost line items to include: (1) Personnel costs — project director, training coordinator, protection officer, field coordinators at Gaziantep/Erbil/Qamishli, finance manager, communications officer; (2) Travel and subsistence — field visits, training delivery, co-applicant coordination; (3) Training and workshop costs — venue hire, materials, per diems for participants, translation; (4) Subcon

Personnel costs must be based on actual salaries documented by employment contracts and payroll records. Use CSIM's existing salary scales as the basis. Avoid inflating staff time allocations — the evaluation committee will scrutinize value for money. Ensure that staff time allocated to the action is not double-counted against other active grants.

Subcontracting must follow PRAG procurement rules. Any subcontract above EUR 10,000 requires at least three quotations; above EUR 60,000 requires a competitive tender. Plan procurement timelines accordingly and include a procurement plan in the full application.

Include a contingency line of no more than 5% of direct costs to cover unforeseen operational expenses, particularly given the volatile security environment in Syria. Label it clearly as contingency and note that it requires prior written approval from the contracting authority before use.

Value for money narrative: given the fixed grant amount, the evaluation will assess whether the proposed activities represent efficient use of EUR 675,000. Benchmark training costs against comparable Syria media development programmes (e.g. Internews Syria, BBC Media Action) and justify unit costs explicitly. Highlight CSIM's cost efficiency from its existing field infrastructure.

Taxes: under EU grant rules, VAT is generally not eligible unless the applicant can demonstrate it cannot recover it. Confirm CSIM's VAT recovery status in Türkiye with the finance team and document accordingly. Field costs incurred inside Syria may have different tax treatment — clarify with the co-applicant.

Budget presentation must follow the standard EU budget template (Annex B of the full application form). Prepare the budget in EUR. For costs incurred in Turkish Lira or Syrian Pounds, use the European Commission's InforEuro exchange rate for the month of submission and document the rate used.
